data.title: Amorolfine (0.25% cream, 5% nail lacquer)
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Other_

**Class:** Morpholine antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits two steps of ergosterol synthesis: Δ14-reductase and Δ7–Δ8 isomerase → ergosterol depletion and toxic sterol build-up
- Fungicidal against dermatophytes; also active against Candida and some moulds

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 0.25% cream: tinea corporis, cruris, pedis; cutaneous candidiasis; pityriasis versicolor
- 5% lacquer: distal and lateral onychomycosis without matrix involvement (up to 2 nails / under 80% nail area), and with oral antifungals for more severe disease

## Dose & formulations
- Cream: once daily (evening) for at least 2–3 weeks, continue 3–5 days after cure
- Lacquer: file the nail, clean with alcohol swab, apply once or twice weekly — 6 months for fingernails, 9–12 months for toenails

## Adverse effects
- Mild burning, itching, erythema
- Lacquer: nail discolouration, brittleness

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; children (limited data for lacquer)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (limited data).

## Viva points
- Morpholine — two enzymes in ergosterol pathway
- Lacquer once weekly (vs ciclopirox daily)
- Not available in the USA; used in India and Europe

_Sources: Khopkar ch.19; Wolverton 4e ch.42 (brief). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
